title: Movie booking domain model
idea: The domain model splits fixed layout (Theatre, Screen, Seat) from per-show state (Show, SeatHold, Booking), with Movie as shared catalog data.

analogy.text: A stadium seating chart versus tonight's ticket list. The chart stays the same for years; every event gets a fresh list of who sits where.
analogy.breaks: A SeatHold expires on its own; a paper list never does.

points: A Theatre has Screens; each Screen has a fixed list of Seats.
A Show plays one Movie on one Screen at one start time.
A SeatHold claims seats of one Show for one user until it expires.
A Booking is created from a SeatHold and carries the price in minor units.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: A Theatre owns one or more Screens. Screens do not move between theatres.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: A Screen owns its Seats. Each Seat has a SeatType that drives its price.

edges.label: uses 1
edges.caption: A Show points at exactly one Screen, so it knows which seats exist.

edges.label: plays 1
edges.caption: A Show plays one Movie. Many Shows can share the same Movie.

edges.label: for 1
edges.caption: A SeatHold belongs to one Show and lists seat ids, not Seat objects.

edges.label: from 1
edges.caption: A Booking is built from one SeatHold and freezes the total price.

edges.label: has
edges.caption: BookingStatus is an enum. The lifecycle page turns it into a state machine.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records for immutable data, a class for Booking because its status changes. Invariants live in constructors.

walk.text: Build the fixed layout: one Movie, one Screen with three Seats, one Theatre.
A Show joins Movie and Screen and sets a price per SeatType, in paise.
Create a hold with a fixed expiry and ask about it at a fixed time.
A Booking is built from the hold; the total comes from Show.priceOf.
Two bad inputs are refused: a seat lookup that fails and an empty hold.
The compact constructor rejects empty holds and copies the list defensively.
Booking is mutable only in status; money is a long, never a double.

pitfalls: Do not store seat state on Seat; one Seat appears in many Shows.
Keep money as long minor units; double rounds 0.1 + 0.2 wrongly.
Validate in constructors so an invalid SeatHold can never exist.

quiz.q: What does the last line of DomainModel print?
options: rejected: no seat Z9 in Audi 1
rejected: a hold needs at least one seat
quiz.why: The second try builds a SeatHold with an empty list. Its compact constructor throws, and the catch prints the message.

takeaway: Fixed layout and per-show state are different classes; keep them apart.

starters: Why is Show not the owner of seat states here?
When should I use a record instead of a class?
How would I model seat categories with different prices per show?
